title: EW and UE Teams
kidRule: English words almost never end in a plain U, so the 'oo' or 'yoo' sound at the end is usually spelled EW or UE. They sound the same, so picture the word to pick the right team! (Menu is a famous rule-breaker.)
hint: I hear an 'oo' or 'yoo' sound, but a plain U cannot do the job here. Which two-letter team does this word use?
reminder: The 'oo' sound here is spelled with a two-letter team: E-W or U-E.

check.question: Why does RESCUE have an E after the U?
check.correctAnswer: English words almost never end in U, so U and E team up at the end!
distractors: Because the E makes the C say its name
Because every long word ends in E

words.def: To save someone or something from danger.
words.sent: Firefighters rescue cats stuck in trees.
words.story: Saint Bernard dogs once helped rescue more than 2,000 travelers who were lost in the snowy Alps!
words.card: That is my *cue* to *rescue* the cat from the pancake pile!

words.def: A curved, creamy nut that is good to eat.
words.sent: I found a cashew in the trail mix.
words.story: A cashew grows hanging from the bottom of a juicy fruit called a cashew apple!
words.card: The squirrel paid *cash* for one giant *cashew*!

words.def: How much something is worth, or how important it is.
words.sent: The old coin has a value of ten dollars.
words.story: A rare postage stamp can have a value of millions of dollars, even though it is just a tiny square of paper!
words.card: Aunt *Val* knows the *value* of every button in her giant button jar!

words.def: To disagree with someone out loud, with each of you saying why you think you are right.
words.sent: My brothers argue about who gets the top bunk.
words.story: This word comes from a Latin word that meant 'to make clear', so a good argument is really about explaining!
words.card: '*Ar*!' said the pirate. 'Never *argue* with a parrot who is holding the map!'

words.def: A shiny, valuable stone like a diamond or a ruby.
words.sent: The crown had a red jewel in the middle.
words.story: The diamond is the hardest jewel of all. Only another diamond can scratch it!
words.card: The *ewe* wore a sparkly *jewel* on each woolly ear!

words.def: A figure of a person or animal made from stone or metal.
words.sent: A statue of a horse stands in the park.
words.story: The Statue of Liberty is made of copper. It was shiny brown at first and slowly turned green!
words.card: The pigeon stuck out its tongue *at* the grumpy *statue*!

words.def: A rule that says what time you must be home or in bed.
words.sent: Our curfew on school nights is eight o'clock.
words.story: Curfew comes from old French words meaning 'cover the fire'. Long ago a bell rang each evening to tell everyone to cover their fires and go to bed!
words.card: Only a *few* owls obeyed the *curfew*, and the rest stayed up telling jokes!

words.def: The son of your brother or sister.
words.sent: My uncle calls me his favorite nephew.
words.story: Donald Duck has three nephews named Huey, Dewey and Louie!
words.card: My *nephew* thinks *he* can teach a hamster to yodel!

words.def: A wide street, often with trees or tall buildings along both sides.
words.sent: The parade marched down the avenue.
words.story: In New York City, most avenues run north and south while the numbered streets run east and west, so the map looks like a grid!
words.card: The ants chose our *avenue* as the *venue* for their picnic parade!

words.def: A meal cooked outdoors over a fire or a grill.
words.sent: We grilled corn at the family barbecue.
words.story: The word barbecue comes from the Taino people of the Caribbean, who cooked food on a wooden frame over a fire!
words.card: The chef waited for his *cue* to flip the *barbecue* pancakes!
